report.tagline: Once India's biggest fantasy cricket app for cash prizes, now a free sports fan app after the 2025 ban on real-money gaming.
report.simpleSummary: Until 2025, Dream11 let you pick a team of real cricketers before a match, pay a small entry fee, and win cash if your players did well. In August 2025, India passed a law banning all online games played for money. Dream11 had to drop paid contests overnight. It is now a free app for following matches with friends, with live scores, commentary, community chat and free contests, and it plans to earn from ads and sponsors.

overview.whatItDoes: Dream11 is a sports app owned by Dream Sports. Before October 2025 it ran fantasy sports contests where users paid to enter and won cash prizes. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 banned every online game with money at stake from 1 October 2025. Dream11 removed all cash contests and relaunched as a free 'second-screen' app you use while watching a match.
howItWorks: You open the app before or during a match and see live scores, stats and commentary.
You can still build a fantasy team, but contests are free and there is no cash prize.
You join community rooms and watch-along streams to chat with other fans live.
The app personalises content around your favourite teams and players using AI.
Dream11 earns from ads and brand sponsorships instead of a cut of entry fees.
Its parent Dream Sports split into eight separate startups, including FanCode and stockbroking app DreamStreet.
overview.valueProposition: Old promise: turn your cricket knowledge into cash. New promise: make watching a match more fun with friends, stats and free games.

businessModel.summary: Dream11 used to make money from one thing: a cut of every paid contest entry. That model is now illegal in India. The new plan is to make money from ads and sponsorships on a free app, which earns far less per user.

revenueStreams.detail: Dream11 kept a share of each entry pool, often estimated at 10% to 20%. This was nearly all of its ₹7,374 crore FY25 revenue and stopped in October 2025.
Ads shown during live matches inside the app.
Brands funding free contests and features.
FanCode (sports streaming and merchandise) and DreamStreet (stockbroking) are now separate startups under Dream Sports.

businessModel.pricing: Free to use since October 2025. No paid contests.
costDrivers: Sports data and rights for live stats
Servers to handle crores of users during big matches
Marketing, though much lower after leaving sponsorships like the BCCI jersey
Staff, cut after more than 100 senior exits and a restructuring
businessModel.unitEconomics: Before the ban: a user paying ₹49 per contest across 100 match days spent about ₹4,900 a year, and Dream11 kept perhaps 15%, roughly ₹700, before the 28% GST hit. After the ban: the same user may see ads worth maybe ₹30 to ₹100 a year to Dream11, based on typical Indian ad rates for app users. That is a fall of roughly 90% in revenue per user, which is why the company had to shrink and split. These are rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Huge existing user base and brand from years of TV ads and team sponsorships
IPL and India match seasons, when cricket interest peaks
Friends inviting friends to free leagues
whatBringsUsersBack: Every match is a new reason to make a team
Personalised alerts for favourite teams and players
growth.moat: Before the ban, the moat was brand, trust in fast payouts and the biggest prize pools. That moat is mostly gone, because prize money is gone. What is left is brand recall, a large list of cricket fans and deep match-data tech. The free app has to win on fun and community, where rivals like JioHotstar and Cricbuzz are strong.

competitors.positioning: Former paid fantasy rivals, also forced to pivot or exit.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: All face the same ban. Dream11 has the biggest brand among them.

competitors.positioning: Where fans already chat about matches.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Dream11 offers structure: teams, points, leaderboards.

pmLessons: If one rule can make your main revenue illegal, regulation is not a side risk, it is the business risk. Plan for it early.
A pivot keeps your users only if the new product still solves their real job. For many users, the job was winning money, not fantasy itself.
Ad-supported apps earn far less per user than paid ones, so the cost base must shrink to match.
Your old moat can disappear overnight. Know which parts of it, like brand and tech, carry over.

interviewQuestions.question: The government bans paid contests tomorrow. You are Dream11's PM. What do you do in the first 90 days?
interviewQuestions.hint: Protect users (refunds, clear messages), keep the habit (free contests), cut costs, test new revenue. Name a metric for each phase.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you make free fantasy sports engaging without cash prizes?
interviewQuestions.hint: Think social status, friends leagues, sponsored rewards, streaks. Measure engagement, not just installs.

interviewQuestions.question: What should the north star metric be after the pivot?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick match-day engaged fans, explain why revenue per user is a guardrail, not the north star.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Dream11 move into a market where paid fantasy is still legal?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh market size, competition (DraftKings, FanDuel in the US), regulation, and whether the brand travels.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you sell Dream11 to advertisers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define audience, engagement time, formats like sponsored contests, proof through case studies.

Post-ban ad revenue per user is an estimate based on typical Indian ad rates.
Registered user figure is from pre-ban company claims; current active users are unknown.
